title: Complete local base change and closed-fibre identification
statement: Let R,A,T be commutative local rings, with T Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let q:R\twoheadrightarrow A and f:R\to T be local ring maps. Let E be a commutative A-algebra and e:T/m_R T\cong E a ring isomorphism such that e(f(r)\bmod m_R T)=q(r) in E for every r. Then C=T\otimes_R A with the canonical right A-algebra structure is Noetherian complete local, A\to C is local, the image of m_T generates m_C, and C/m_A C\cong E as A-algebras.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs), the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

proof.text: Let I=ker(R→A). Locality puts I in m_R and its extension in m_T, so T/IT is nonzero. The quotient-kernel algebra equivalence and tensor-quotient equivalence identify T/IT with C=T tensor_R A (lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change). Surjectivity of T→C then gives a local Noetherian ring and m_T C=m_C by Mathlib IsLocalRing.of_surjective', isNoetherianRing_of_surjective, and map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs), the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

proof.text: Since T→C is surjective, C is a finite T-module. Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian to m_T and C. Mathlib IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff and m_T C=m_C identify this with m_C-adic completeness. To prove A→C local, lift a to r∈R; if its image is a unit, locality of T→C and R→T makes r a unit, hence a is a unit.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs), the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

proof.text: Give E its induced R-algebra structure. Compose T→T/m_R T with e and tensor this R-algebra map with A→E to obtain an A-algebra map F:C→E, F(t tensor a)=e(t mod m_R T) times a. Compatibility he checks the R-algebra relation, and the formula on 1 tensor a checks A-linearity. The composite T→C→E is e after the quotient map and is surjective, hence F is surjective. As T→C is surjective, ker F is the image of its pullback to T, namely m_R T. The equality q(m_R)=m_A and equality of the two maps R→C identify this image with m_A C. Apply the quotient-kernel algebra equivalence to F and transport along this ideal equality to get C/m_A C ≅ E. This is the proved private closed-fibre helper; it does not assume Noetherianity or completeness.
